questions.prompt: Which members of an object does `XmlSerializer` write to XML?
options: Its public fields and properties, but not methods, private fields or read-only properties
All fields and properties, including private ones, but not methods
Its public methods and properties, but not fields
questions.explanation: XML serialization converts an object's public state (fields and properties) into XML; it does not include methods, private fields or read-only properties.

questions.prompt: Ignoring the `<?xml ...?>` declaration and whitespace, what XML does this write to `person.xml`?
questions.explanation: `XmlSerializer` uses the class and member names by default, and public fields become elements, so the output is `<Person>` with `<Name>` and `<Age>` children.

questions.prompt:
In this class, `ID` is marked `[XmlAttribute]`. How is a `Product` with `ID = 123` serialized?

`public class Product { [XmlAttribute] public int ID; public string Name; }`
questions.explanation: `[XmlAttribute]` serializes that one member as an XML attribute; the other public members stay elements by default.

questions.prompt: A `Team` class has `[XmlArray("Players")]` and `[XmlArrayItem("Player")]` on its `List<string> Members`. What does the list serialize to?
questions.explanation: `[XmlArray]` renames the outer wrapper element and `[XmlArrayItem]` renames each item, giving `<Players><Player>…</Player></Players>`.

questions.prompt: You want an `XmlWriter` to write an XML fragment that has no single root element. Which `XmlWriterSettings` property do you change?
questions.explanation: `ConformanceLevel` is `Document` by default; the lesson says to use `Fragment` for writing fragments (no root). `OmitXmlDeclaration` only drops the `<?xml ... ?>` prolog.

questions.prompt: In `<order xmlns="http://example.com/order"><name>John</name></order>`, what namespace does the unprefixed `<name>` element belong to?
options: No namespace, because it has no prefix
A namespace named `order`, taken from the parent element
No namespace until it is declared with `xmlns:name`
questions.explanation: A namespace declared without a prefix is the default: all child elements without their own prefix belong to it (attributes, however, don't inherit it).
